text:
Hannah: Heads-up: staging linkcheck failed after the docs repo move. A couple of TOC links and an inline image are 404ing.

LinkCheckerBot: linkcheck result: build #611 failed at step linkcheck - https://ci.redwood/611 :x: 

Hannah: Log excerpt:
```
WARN Broken fragment: /tutorials/quickstart.md#using-the-console -> fragment not found
ERROR Missing asset: /docs/assets/screens/console-screenshot.png -> 404
WARN Broken fragment: /reference/api.md#response-formatting -> fragment not found
```

Marco: I ran a local slug scan. Two issues I see: (1) the MDX slugifier merged nested headings like `Using the console` under `Quickstart` into `#quickstart-using-the-console` whereas previous MkDocs generated `#using-the-console` (2) the screenshot was moved to `static/screens/console-screenshot.png` but many files still use bundled relative paths under `docs/assets/` which no longer exist in the built site.

Ivy: Also spotted one weird corner: a code fence immediately above a heading can suppress the generated anchor in our MDX pipeline if the fence isn't followed by a blank line. That caused `#response-formatting` to not be created in api.md. We had one heading like:

```
```python
# example
```
### Response formatting
```
\nwhich needs a blank line after the fence.

DevDocs: Suggested fixes: 
- Update internal refs to the new slug pattern OR add explicit short ids on target headings for backward compatibility (preferred for public headings).
- Canonicalize static images under `/screens/` (site-root) and update refs to `/screens/console-screenshot.png`.
- Fix MDX code-fence spacing to ensure anchors are generated.
- Add a small CI test that validates fragments for changed files only.

Hannah: How many refs are broken?

Marco: Grep results: `rg "#using-the-console|#response-formatting" --hidden docs/` -> 5 hits total (3 in tutorials, 2 in examples). Also a couple of external blog posts link to `#using-the-console` (low volume).

Ivy: Proposed plan: 
1) Update the 5 internal refs to the slugs produced by the new pipeline (`#quickstart-using-the-console` and `#r-response-formatting` — concrete values determined by slugify rules)
2) Add explicit legacy ids on the two target headings to preserve external links, e.g. `### Using the console {#using-the-console}` and `### Response formatting {#response-formatting}`
3) Replace relative image paths with site-root `/screens/console-screenshot.png` and add a short note in contributor guide about where static assets live now.
4) Add `tests/changed_fragment_check.sh` to run in CI for changed files only.

Marco: Small nit: the slugifier turned headings that begin with uppercase single-letter tokens into `r-` prefixes (so `Response formatting` became `r-response-formatting`) — that's from the slugify library handling single-letter words. I'd rather add explicit ids for readability.

Hannah: Agreed, explicit ids are clearer and cheap. If external blogs exist we keep compatibility. For internal-only links we'll update to the slugified target to avoid duplication.

DevDocs: Checklist for the PR:
- [ ] Update 5 internal references to current slugs
- [ ] Add explicit legacy ids on two headings in `tutorials/quickstart.md` and `reference/api.md`
- [ ] Fix the code-fence blank line in `reference/api.md` so the anchor is generated reliably
- [ ] Move/update image paths to `/screens/console-screenshot.png` and ensure `static/screens` contains the file
- [ ] Add `tests/changed_fragment_check.sh` and wire it into CI for PRs
- [ ] Add a short migration note in `docs/MIGRATION.md` about slug differences and the static asset canonical path

Hannah: I'll open a single small PR that does the ref updates, adds the explicit ids, fixes the code fence spacing, and updates the image path. Ivy can add the check script in a follow-up if that's ok.

Ivy: I'll prepare the check script and a tiny README snippet about asset placement under `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`. PR for the script after the link fixes.

Marco: Please also update the Python SDK example in `examples/python/console_demo.py` — it links to the quickstart heading.

Hannah: PR 1001 opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1001 - includes: updated fragment refs (5 files), explicit heading ids, fixed code fence blank line, updated image path to `/screens/console-screenshot.png`, and a migration note in MIGRATION.md. Ran `pnpm docs:build` and `pnpm docs:linkcheck` locally.

LinkCheckerBot: PR 1001 - linkcheck queued.

Marco: Ran linkcheck locally against the branch; fragments present and image resolves. Added a tiny unit that checks for blank-line-before-heading after code fences.

LinkCheckerBot: CI for PR 1001 - linkcheck passed :white_check_mark:. Full build green.

Hannah: Merged. Staging site now shows the console screenshot and the broken fragments are resolved.

Ivy: Opening follow-up PR with `tests/changed_fragment_check.sh` and an update to `CONTRIBUTING.md` that explains using `/screens/` for screenshots.

DevDocs: Follow-ups filed: 
- infra ticket for pre-commit hook to run `tests/changed_fragment_check.sh`
- docs task to canonicalize `static/screens` folder and clean old `docs/assets` references

Hannah: Thanks all. Closing thread. :tada:
